lessons.title: Lesson 1.1
lessons.contentBody:
On the job

Lesson 1. A kitchen in Townsville flooded overnight when a flexible hose under the sink split. The owner found 10 mm of water across the vinyl at 6 am and called the insurer, who called you. Two children live in the house and the family wants to stay.

The idea

Moisture moves from wet materials to drier air. The drier the air around a wet wall, the faster the wall gives up its water. That is why a technician measures the air as well as the materials, and records both on every visit. A reading on its own means little; a reading compared with a dry reference in the same building tells you how far the job has to go. Pick a dry reference on the same material, in a room that was not affected, and write down where it is so the next visit uses the same spot.

Moisture moves from wet materials to drier air. The drier the air around a wet wall, the faster the wall gives up its water. That is why a technician measures the air as well as the materials, and records both on every visit. A reading on its own means little; a reading compared with a dry reference in the same building tells you how far the job has to go. Pick a dry reference on the same material, in a room that was not affected, and write down where it is so the next visit uses the same spot.

Moisture moves from wet materials to drier air. The drier the air around a wet wall, the faster the wall gives up its water. That is why a technician measures the air as well as the materials, and records both on every visit. A reading on its own means little; a reading compared with a dry reference in the same building tells you how far the job has to go. Pick a dry reference on the same material, in a room that was not affected, and write down where it is so the next visit uses the same spot.

Moisture moves from wet materials to drier air. The drier the air around a wet wall, the faster the wall gives up its water. That is why a technician measures the air as well as the materials, and records both on every visit. A reading on its own means little; a reading compared with a dry reference in the same building tells you how far the job has to go. Pick a dry reference on the same material, in a room that was not affected, and write down where it is so the next visit uses the same spot.

See it

The diagram shows where to take readings along the wall.

Do it in metric

The room is 4.0 m by 3.0 m, so the floor area is 12 m². At 2.4 m ceiling height the volume is 28.8 m³. A dehumidifier rated at 50 L/day at 30 °C and 80% RH will remove less water on a cooler day, so plan on about 30 L/day and check the logged readings each visit.

Field download

Download the moisture map card and fill in one row per reading point.

Check yourself

Answer the three questions in the module check before you move on.

Takeaway

Measure the air and the materials, compare with a dry reference, and write it down every visit. Next: setting a drying goal.
